meta.name: Nevil Ghelani
meta.title: Senior Application Developer · Agentic AI & Multi-Agent Systems
meta.summary: Senior Application Developer at ADP specializing in agentic AI and multi-agent system orchestration. Built a Copilot-based AI debugging agent with access to 50+ enterprise repositories, created as a self-initiated project and now in use by developers on the team. Independently built a prototype SMS agent that books HVAC service appointments from missed calls (tested with a test business; not deployed) and JARVIS, a rule-bounded multi-agent system that builds small software applications. Research focus: measuring whether AI agents that answer calls for small HVAC businesses handle life-safety calls, such as gas leaks and carbon-monoxide symptoms, correctly. Co-inventor on a granted Indian patent for a vision-based robot.

proposedEndeavor.headline: Measuring How AI Agents Handle Life-Safety Calls
proposedEndeavor.subtitle: Planned research: open, reproducible tests of whether AI agents that answer calls for small HVAC businesses tell emergencies apart from routine jobs and give callers the right safety instructions.
paragraphs: Small HVAC businesses are starting to use AI agents to answer calls, book jobs, and notify technicians. Most calls are routine, but some are not: a caller who smells gas, or who has carbon-monoxide symptoms, must be told to get to safety and call the gas utility or 911, as federal agencies, state fire officials, and gas utilities instruct. I have found no published, independent evaluation of how reliably these agents handle such calls.

My research plan starts with an open test set of realistic calls, each labeled against official safety guidance, and scoring software that reports how many life-safety calls an agent misses and how many routine calls it wrongly escalates. I plan to publish the test set, the software, and the results, and then to measure, with a collaborator experienced in field studies, how much of a small-shop technician's or owner's day front-desk tasks take.

The work builds on what I already do: building AI agents and the software that checks what they do. That includes an AI debugging agent at ADP, a prototype SMS booking agent for HVAC businesses, and JARVIS, a personal research project in which rules written in ordinary code bound what the AI agents may do.

impactPoints.title: Safety Guidance as the Answer Key
impactPoints.description: Each test call is labeled with the response that official guidance prescribes, such as leaving the building and calling the gas utility or 911 for a gas odor.

impactPoints.title: Measured, Not Assumed
impactPoints.description: Scoring software reports missed life-safety calls, unnecessary escalations, and whether each booking is correct, for any agent tested.

impactPoints.title: Openly Published
impactPoints.description: The test set, scoring method, and results are planned to be public, so contractors, software makers, and standards bodies can use and check them.

research.title: Agentic AI for HVAC Missed-Call Recovery and Scheduling (Prototype)
research.tagline: LangGraph SMS agent · tested with a test business; not deployed
highlights: Built an LLM-based SMS agent for HVAC businesses: when a call goes unanswered, the caller hears an automated message and then receives a text from the agent, which converses with the customer to book a service appointment.

Implemented the agent as a LangGraph state machine with specialized nodes for booking, rescheduling, confirmation and escalation; it reads a configured business's hours, location and truck count and checks its Google Calendar to book jobs automatically, without staff involvement.

research.title: JARVIS: Rule-Bounded Multi-Agent Orchestration for Software Engineering
research.tagline: Personal research project · one operator, not yet benchmarked
highlights: Built a system in which AI agents plan, design, code and check small Python applications from a plain-English brief, then run them on a schedule inside a sandbox.
Rules written in ordinary code, not the AI, decide which next step is allowed; a separate verifier re-runs the reported commands and checks each requirement before any model judges the result.
Serves one operator on a single machine; two apps it built are in regular use; not yet benchmarked.

research.tagline: “An Autonomous Robot,” Indian Patent No. 578389 · co-invented with three fellow students and faculty advisor
highlights: Integrated the OAK-D stereo camera for real-time object detection on a dual-controller edge-computing robot (Nvidia Jetson Nano for spatial AI, Arduino for mechanical kinematics).
Built the robot's mobile app integration; the team's robot navigated semi-autonomously by reading ArUco markers placed along its route, with YOLOv3 object detection.
Gained foundational experience in real-time data processing on edge hardware.
